verdict.reasoning:
The claim's raw observations about the markdown file check out, but they do not constitute a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy, and the claim's asserted harm does not exist.

What I confirmed independently:
(1) The rendered page (E:/Temp/specrecon/v422/spec_p422.png, printed folio 392) shows 13.18.16.2 General format as an ordinary in-flow two-row figure: outer brace pair over 'CONTROL IS' / 'CONTROLS ARE', a second independent brace pair over '{ data-name-1 } ...' / 'FINAL [ data-name-1 ] ...'. Reading the printed glyphs directly, CONTROL, CONTROLS and FINAL each carry an underline; IS and ARE do not. The ellipsis after '{ data-name-1 }' and after '[ data-name-1 ]' are both present. Every one of these facts is faithfully carried by the markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 18075-18080 and by its figure-notes paragraph. The transcription of the DIAGRAM ITSELF is correct and complete — nothing is added, dropped, weakened or strengthened.
(2) The markdown really is blockquote-wrapped: line 18075 is '> ```', lines 18076-18077 are '> '-prefixed, line 18078 is '> ```', and line 18080 is '> > **Figure notes (CONTROL clause general format).**'.
(3) The scale figures are right: exactly 20 lines in the file match '^> ```' (= 10 blockquoted figures), 215 figure-notes paragraphs use the single-level '> **Figure notes' form, and 10 use the '> > ' form — i.e. the two counts are consistent with each other, so the 10 blockquoted figures are internally self-consistent as a group (each blockquoted fence is paired with a doubly-quoted note, never mismatched).
(4) The very next figure, 13.18.17.2 DEFAULT clause (the claim's page 424), does use a bare ``` fence and a single-level note, so the local inconsistency the claim describes is genuine.

Why this is nonetheless rejected:
(a) It is not a discrepancy between the PDF and the transcription. The PDF has no notion of a blockquote; blockquote-vs-bare-fence is a choice that exists only on the markdown side. Both forms transcribe the same in-flow figure, and the claim itself concedes 'No syntax information is lost.' This is markdown internal styling inconsistency, not lost or altered spec content. It falls squarely under the rejection criterion 'the difference is only ... formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning.'
(b) The claimed downstream harm is hypothetical and, as of this tree, false. I searched scripts/spec/ (build_inventory.py, extract_rule_catalog.py, gen_conformance_notes.py, merge_reconciliation.py, page_workunit.py) and the wider scripts/ tree for any figure-extraction logic keying on a line equal to '```' (patterns strip() == '```' and startswith('```')): there are no matches. The only ``` occurrences in gen_conformance_notes.py are literal ```dataview fences it emits into Obsidian output, unrelated to reading the spec. No extraction pass 'will skip this diagram entirely' because no such pass exists.
(c) The rendering complaint overstates the effect. Because the fence AND its note are both shifted one level together, the note's indent RELATIVE to its own figure is identical to every sibling; only the whole figure-plus-note unit sits one level deeper. That is a uniform shift of a self-consistent 10-figure sub-convention, not a note detached from its figure.

Bottom line: the diagram, its choice indicators, its underlining, its brace structure and its ellipses are all transcribed correctly. Nothing about the standard's content differs between the two sources. If someone wants the 10 blockquoted figures normalized to the 215-figure majority style, that is a cosmetic housekeeping chore on the markdown, not a spec-reconciliation finding.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The 13.18.16.2 CONTROL clause figure is transcribed correctly and completely (brace pairs, ellipses, and the CONTROL/CONTROLS/FINAL underlining vs un-underlined IS/ARE all verified against the rendered page). The only true observation is a markdown-internal style inconsistency: 10 of 225 general-format figures in specs/ISO_COBOL.md — this one among them — wrap the fence and its notes in a blockquote ('> ```' plus '> > **Figure notes ...**') instead of the majority bare-fence form. The group is internally consistent (all 10 blockquoted fences pair with all 10 doubly-quoted notes), no spec content is affected, and the asserted breakage of a fence-keyed figure-extraction pass is unfounded — no such pass exists anywhere in scripts/.
